Check a project folder for files that look like USRDS data

Source: R/check_repo_for_usrds_data.R
check_repo_for_usrds_data.Rd

Scans a project folder, usually a git repository, for files that look like patient-level USRDS data, so they can be removed or ignored before they are committed or shared. USRDS data are covered by a data use agreement: a private repository is still a disclosure.

Usage

check_repo_for_usrds_data(path = ".", id_columns = "USRDS_ID", quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

path

The project folder to check. Defaults to the working directory.

id_columns

Column names that identify a patient. A text file whose header has any of them is reported. The default is "USRDS_ID"; add SRTR identifiers such as "PX_ID" or "PERS_ID" when the project also uses SRTR data.

quiet

If TRUE, nothing is printed.

Value

A data frame with one row per file reported and columns path (relative to path) and reason, invisibly. Its scan attribute is "git" or "folder", saying which list of files was checked.

Details

A file is reported when it is:

  • a data file type: .sas7bdat, .sas7bcat, .xpt, .parquet, .feather, .arrow, .dta or .sav;

  • named like a USRDS file (an Appendix B file name, with any year, or a claim file the package reads), with a .csv, .tsv, .txt, .rds, .rda, .rdata, .xls or .xlsx extension; or

  • a .csv, .tsv or .txt file whose header line has a column in id_columns (case ignored).

Inside a git repository, the files checked are those git would commit: tracked files, and untracked files that .gitignore does not exclude. A file git already tracks is checked even if .gitignore lists it. Outside one, or when git is not installed, every file under path is checked, apart from the .git folder. Files under tests/testthat/fixtures/ whose names start with synthetic- are skipped, as made-up test data.

The check is read-only. It reads file names, and the first line of .csv, .tsv and .txt files to find column names. It does not read any other content, and it reports paths only.

A clean result does not make a folder safe: data can sit in files with other names or formats. See the article "Data protection and security" on the package website.

Examples

project <- tempfile("project")
dir.create(project)
writeLines(c("USRDS_ID,age", "1,50"), file.path(project, "cohort.csv"))
writeLines("x <- 1", file.path(project, "analysis.R"))
check_repo_for_usrds_data(project)
#> Warning: 1 file in /tmp/RtmpcSCEIw/project18bb701c27da may be USRDS data:
#> • cohort.csv: identifier column (USRDS_ID)
#> ℹ Checked all files (not a git repository, or git not found).
#> ℹ Move these files outside the project, or list untracked ones in .gitignore.
#> ℹ .gitignore does not stop git tracking a file it already tracks; remove such
#>   files from git with `git rm --cached <file>`. Data already pushed needs
#>   separate remediation.
unlink(project, recursive = TRUE)
